subject: Re: Pilot safety-net & surge provisioning credit request
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alexis Torres <alexis@clearvista.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot safety-net and surge provisioning ask

Alexis —

Thanks again for the demo last week. ClearVista's usage patterns during the live test look promising, and we want to make sure you don't hit capacity limits while you evaluate integration with internal tooling. A few asks from your side came up:

- A short-term "safety-net" credit to cover unexpected surge tokens / concurrency during the two-week evaluation extension.
- A written runbook for scale events and an SLA-friendly fallback model during the pilot.

We can do a one-time safety-net credit that only applies to burst/surge consumption (not baseline usage), plus a short addendum that documents how we'll route requests if dedicated capacity spikes. That lets you keep the environment stable while you finish feature validation.

Attached is a short term-sheet outlining the safety-net proposal and the minimal operational runbook (redwood_safety-net-term-sheet.pdf). If that looks reasonable, I can loop in Kimberly (sales lead) and Marissa (solutions) to finalize commercials and get procurement the paperwork.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm the maximum surge we should cover (suggested starting point: +40% over observed peak).
2) We send an addendum and DocuSign.
3) Once executed, we apply the safety-net credit and enable the scale routing policy.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you'd prefer.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_safety-net-term-sheet.pdf

From: Alexis Torres <alexis@clearvista.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot safety-net and surge provisioning ask

On Thu, Jul 10, 2025 at 9:12 AM Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alexis —
> 
> Thanks again for the demo last week...

Thanks Sean — this is exactly what we were hoping for. A couple clarifying points from our ops and procurement teams: 

- We'd prefer the safety-net to be structured as a "surge bucket" that is consumed before billable tokens so we can validate integration without surprise charges.
- Can the credit be scoped to specific project IDs so we don't need to change other teams' usage?
- Procurement would like to see a simple acceptance criterion before closing the addendum: 3 successful scale events with live traffic within the extended pilot window.

We attached our internal requirements doc (clearvista_requirements.pdf) to this reply. If you can accommodate project-level scoping and the acceptance criterion, we can route to procurement and sign quickly.

—Alexis
Alexis Torres
Head of ML Integrations | ClearVista
alexis@clearvista.ai
Attachments: clearvista_requirements.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-11T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot safety-net and surge provisioning ask

Sean —

Saw Alexis' note. Two quick internal points:
1) We can do project-scoped surge buckets (tagged at the API key level); Marissa, can you confirm technical constraints for enforcement?
2) Commercially, let's make the safety-net a capped, non-recurring credit that expires at pilot end. We'll want to avoid open-ended commitments.

I recommend we offer: up to $6k in surge credits scoped to two project IDs, with a conversion cadence where any sustained usage beyond the cap rolls into normal pay-as-you-go (or we discuss a committed reserve). Also agree to the acceptance criterion (3 successful scale events) and operational runbook.

If Alexis/procurement accepts, draft the addendum and include the acceptance test and the project ID scoping language. I'll OK the concession.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alexis Torres <alexis@clearvista.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@clearvista.com
Date: 2025-07-12T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot safety-net and surge provisioning ask

Alexis —

Thanks for the quick reply and the requirements doc. We can do exactly what Kimberly outlined:

- One-time surge credit: $6,000, scoped to two ClearVista project IDs (we'll enforce by API key tags).
- Credit applies only to burst/surge consumption above historical baseline for the pilot projects, and will be consumed first before any billable usage.
- Acceptance criterion: 3 successful scale events within the extended pilot window (we'll timestamp and capture logs that both teams can review).
- Operational runbook and routing policy (attached).

I've prepared a slim addendum that includes the surge-credit table, the project scoping language, and the acceptance criteria. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/clearvista-redwood-clv57 (please route to procurement). If procurement needs a PO-first flow, let us know — we can also do a short-term invoice to clear the paperwork quickly.

Next steps:
1) Alexis: confirm the two project IDs you want covered and the procurement contact for signature.
2) We send DocuSign; once countersigned we apply the credit and enable scale routing.

If you'd prefer a quick call to walk procurement through the addendum, Kimberly and I can join.

Best,
Sean
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Attachments: redwood_safety-net-term-sheet.pdf (updated)

Thanks Sean — this works for us. Confirming the two project IDs to cover: CV-frontend-02 and CV-inference-stage. Procurement contact is procurement@clearvista.com.

Appreciate the flexibility — this should remove a major blocker for us continuing the evaluation.

—Alexis
